title: Origin
body:
An origin is the triple **scheme + host + port**. All three must match for two URLs to be same-origin. `https://app.example.com` and `https://api.example.com` are different origins (different host); so are `http://example.com` and `https://example.com` (different scheme), and `https://example.com` and `https://example.com:8080` (different port).

The path does *not* participate — `https://example.com/a` and `https://example.com/b` are the same origin. This definition is the unit that the [[Same-Origin Policy]] and [[CORS]] both operate on, and it's also roughly the boundary cookies and [[localStorage]] are scoped to. Note "site" is a looser concept than "origin", and `SameSite` cookies use the site definition rather than this one.
